summary: Malicious font CDN stylesheet triggered server-side font-proxy fetch and leaked service token
description: Issue summary: At 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC automated anomaly detection flagged a spike in requests authenticated with the internal service identity help-center-font-proxy@redwood-svc. The requests originated from unrelated IP ranges and targeted internal API endpoints. Impact: Possible short-lived exposure of a service token used by our server-side font proxy. No confirmed data exfiltration of customer content; potential read-only calls to internal metrics APIs were observed. Environment: Help Center frontend (prod, us-east) uses a server-side font-proxy service that fetches remote font files and serves them to clients to avoid CORS and external tracking in browsers.
detection_timeline: 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Alert fired (abnormal token usage). 2026-03-10 02:13 UTC - Initial ACK by on-call security. 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC - Scoped affected token and blocked further use. 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Rotated help-center-font-proxy service token and invalidated prior sessions. 2026-03-11 09:40 UTC - Additional traffic observed from attacker-controlled domains; blocked at WAF. 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - Ongoing forensic analysis; ticket updated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Load the Help Center page which references fonts via third-party CDN. 2) The CDN returned a malicious stylesheet containing an @font-face rule whose src pointed at a URL hosted on an attacker-controlled domain. 3) The server-side font-proxy (font-proxy.redwood.internal) was invoked to fetch the remote resource on behalf of the client and included the service token in the Authorization header (legacy behavior). 4) Attacker received the proxied request and recorded the Authorization header value and then attempted reuse against internal endpoints.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: compromised 3rd-party font CDN returned crafted stylesheet to cause server-side proxy fetches.

Confirmed evidence: proxy request logs show outbound fetch to https://malicious-fonts[.]example with Authorization: Bearer <token> and response status 200. The same token was then used in subsequent requests to /internal/metrics and /admin/status endpoints from unrelated IPs.

Token use: observed ~42 distinct requests over 6 minutes from ~18 IPs in 3 cloud provider regions. Most calls were read-only; 3 attempts to query service account metadata were blocked by internal IAM filters.
Detection sources: proxy access logs (kibana link), cloud egress logs (cloudflare), WAF alerts, internal SIEM correlation (Splunk link).

Root cause hypothesis: legacy proxy behavior added Authorization headers to outbound font fetches without origin filtering. Vendor CDN was compromised (or had a malicious ad insertion) and returned attacker-hosted font src URLs.
Evidence artifacts: saved malicious stylesheet sample, outbound request capture, attacker IP list recorded to security bucket (s3://sec-artifacts/INT-601820/).
mitigation_actions: Immediate: Rotated help-center-font-proxy service token and invalidated old keys (2026-03-10 03:05 UTC).
Immediate: Deployed WAF rule to block outbound egress to the attacker IPs/domains and added an emergency denylist for malicious-fonts[.]example (2026-03-10 03:30 UTC).
Short-term: Disabled server-side font-proxy remote fetch for third-party origins; serving only cached/approved fonts (2026-03-10 04:00 UTC).
Medium-term: Patch to proxy to drop Authorization headers for outbound requests to untrusted origins and add allowlist for internal services (PR linked).
Monitoring: Added SIEM alert for any token usage outside the approved IP ranges for service identities.
related_github_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8241 (font-proxy: stop forwarding auth to third-party origins)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8245 (help-center: pin fonts to vetted CDN list)

resolution: Partial mitigations applied: token rotated, outbound egress blocked to attacker domains, server-side font-proxy disabled for unvetted origins. Hotfix PR merged to drop Authorization on outbound proxy fetches; staged rollout started. Full forensic report pending. No customer data confirmed exfiltrated as of last update.
next_steps: Complete forensic timeline and publish post-incident report (owner: Sec Ops) by 2026-03-18.
Roll out proxied-auth hotfix to all regions and enforce allowlist for proxy origins (owner: Platform Infra).
Coordinate with Vendor Risk to notify the third-party CDN and confirm compromise/mitigation with their security team.
Add automated unit/integration tests to prevent credential forwarding regressions in the proxy codepath.
Schedule a tabletop review with Security, SRE, Product (Help Center owners) and Developer Experience to review design choices.
